claims.text: The corrosion behavior of pre-exposed Q235 steel is primarily dictated by the integrity and composition of its naturally formed passive oxide film.
A continuous, defect-free oxide layer suppresses localized corrosion.
The oxide layer suppresses corrosion by impeding ion and electron transfer.
Defects or discontinuities in the oxide film serve as initiation sites for accelerated corrosion.
The corrosion-promoting effects of oxide-film defects become more pronounced at elevated temperatures.
As-received Q235 mild steel has an intact native thin passive oxide film composed mainly of Fe2O3 and Fe3O4.
Controlled mechanical abrasion will introduce defects into the surface oxide.
Chemical passivation or mild annealing will enhance oxide-film uniformity.
A uniform oxide film limits corrosive-ion access and electron exchange.
Limiting ion access and electron exchange suppresses anodic iron dissolution.
Film discontinuities create localized anodic sites that accelerate corrosion through preferential dissolution.
Higher temperature amplifies the proposed corrosion mechanism through increased reaction rates and ion mobility.
Samples with an intact, uniform oxide film will have lower corrosion rates than samples with deliberately introduced surface defects.
Samples with an intact, uniform oxide film will have fewer pitting sites than samples with deliberately introduced surface defects.
The difference in degradation between intact-film and defect-containing samples will be greater at 70°C than at approximately 25°C.
Electrochemical testing can be used to assess corrosion behavior in a sodium chloride solution.
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy will evaluate passive-film integrity.
The quantitative relationship between oxide-film defect density and corrosion rate is not fully delineated.
The temperature threshold for accelerated oxide-film breakdown may vary with environmental chemistry.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis refers to 'pre-exposed Q235 steel,' whereas the material initial state describes as-received steel in a 'pre-exposure' state. These denote different exposure histories unless 'pre-exposed' is a wording error.
